questions.stem: What is the reason a shadow is formed?
choices: Light is reflected by an object
Light is absorbed by an object
Light is blocked by an object
Light is scattered by an object
questions.solution: Light is blocked by an object, which prevents it from reaching a surface, creating a shadow. Reflection occurs when light bounces off a surface, absorption occurs when light is taken in by a material, and scattering happens when light spreads out in different directions. None of these directly cause a shadow to form.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the image formed by a plane mirror?
choices: It is always smaller than the object
It is always the same size as the object
questions.solution: The image formed by a plane mirror is always the same size as the object. A pupil might think the image is inverted or smaller due to a misconception about how mirrors work. The image is erect, not upside down, and does not change size with distance from the mirror.

questions.stem: A person is looking at their image in a plane mirror. If they move their right hand forward, which hand does the image move?
questions.solution: The image formed by a plane mirror shows lateral inversion, meaning the left and right sides are reversed. So, if a person moves their right hand forward, the image will appear to move its left hand. A pupil might think the image moves the same hand due to a misunderstanding of lateral inversion.

questions.stem: Why is the Moon not considered a luminous object?
choices: It reflects light from the Sun
It is made of dark material
It is too far from the Earth
questions.solution: The Moon is not considered a luminous object because it does not produce its own light. Instead, it reflects sunlight, which makes it visible from Earth. The other options are incorrect because emitting its own light would make it luminous, being made of dark material does not determine luminosity, and distance does not affect whether an object is luminous.

headingPath: 11.2 Does Light Travel in a Straight Line?

questions.stem: In a pinhole camera, the image of an object is formed on a screen. What is the nature of the image formed?
questions.solution: The image formed by a pinhole camera is always inverted because light travels in straight lines, and the pinhole allows only a narrow beam of light to reach the screen, resulting in an upside-down image. The other options are incorrect because the image is not always upright or only sometimes inverted; it is consistently inverted due to the geometry of light propagation.

questions.critique: The solution is correct. A pinhole camera forms an inverted image because light travels in straight lines, and the pinhole only allows a narrow beam of light to pass through, resulting in an upside-down image on the screen. The correct answer is 1.
